{{Quote|You're just a little gravel maggot!|Mawhonic taunts a rival|translated=1|audio=Mawhonic-taunt.flac|<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: Racer">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']]</ref>}}
'''Mawhonic''' {{Pronounced|mɑ'hɑnɪk}} was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] who hailed from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Hok/Legends|Hok]]. By the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Mawhonic was an accomplished [[Podracer/Legends|Podracer]] [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|pilot]], with fame on worlds such as [[Ando Prime/Legends|Ando Prime]], [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]], and [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]. Using a [[Color/Legends|green]] [[Galactic Power Engineering/Legends|Galactic Power Engineering]] [[GPE-3130 Podracer/Legends|GPE-3130]] Podracer, Mawhonic soared through the sport with several record times. In addition to racing, Mawhonic also struck out a living selling Podracer parts. Mawhonic participated in the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Boonta Eve Classic (32 BBY)/Legends|of 32 BBY]], which was based out of the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] planet of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. The Gran started on the front row, and during the first lap, Mawhonic's 3130 was destroyed by the [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]].

Despite the perceived severity of the crash, Mawhonic survived and later took part in the [[Vinta Harvest Classic/Legends|Vinta Harvest Classic]] race on Malastare. Although he was the local crowd favorite, Mawhonic lost another race to Sebulba. Furious about Sebulba's attempt to kill him in the Boonta, Mawhonic posted bounties on several of Sebulba's relatives, accepting them either [[Death/Legends|dead]] or alive. Several years later, Mawhonic, still [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] a GPE Podracer, joined the [[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]] racing season. Mawhonic held two speed records, and also displayed his aggressive side when he made it onto competitor knockout charts. Mawhonic's career extended into the year [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], where the Podracing courses extended into worlds such as [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]] and [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].

==Biography==
[[File:Mawhonic-DB.png|thumb|left|250px|Mawhonic, in his [[Podracer/Legends|Podracer]].]]
In addition to being a [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|pilot]], Mawhonic was a [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]] parts dealer. He could often be found in his shop where his [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series astromech droid]] frequently worked on his podracer. The [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] was willing to sell parts for [[Hutt/Legends|Huttese]] [[Currency/Legends|currency]] or to trade parts, but he refused to accept [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|Republic credit]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace (video game)">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref>

He was one of only a handful of racers, including [[Gasgano/Legends|Gasgano]], that [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]] ever counted as a real threat to his career. Sebulba's loathing of Mawhonic was likely supplemented by the fact that the three-eyed alien was of the Gran race, the very same species that had enslaved Sebulba's people, the [[Dug/Legends|Dugs]], on their home [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]]. Mawhonic would become vicious whenever Sebulba was around, whereas otherwise he was quite good-natured.

An unspoken alliance between Mawhonic and Gasgano revealed itself whenever they were racing against Sebulba: if an opportunity to work together to bring the Dug down presented itself, they would do so. However, they rarely had anything to do with each other in their off hours, as each found the other's personality detestable. In the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] of [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Mawhonic's Podracer was destroyed in the first lap by Sebulba as they were passing through the [[Mushroom Mesa/Legends|Mushroom Mesa]].

[[File:Mawhonic_Racer.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Mawhonic's GPE-3130 podracer.]]

Soon after the race, a maddened Mawhonic pronounced his hatred for Sebulba and his family. He put a bounty on at least two of the cheating Dug's relatives, [[Nebulba]] and [[Xijulba]] of Malastare's [[Sebolto]] Clan. The [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], would eventually snag the bounties while on the planet, although it is still unclear whether they were taken alive or dead.<ref name="SW:BH">''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]''</ref>

Mawhonic returned later on to compete in Malastare's [[Vinta Harvest Classic/Legends|Vinta Harvest Classic]], apparently no worse for wear. During this race, he was introduced by [[Fodesinbeed Annodue/Legends|Fode and Beed]] as the local Gran favourite. Astonished, Sebulba accused him of being an impostor, but all evidence pointed to the fact that he was genuine. Rumors began to fly around that there had been an impostor Mawhonic, but this had been the one who perished in the Boonta Eve Classic&mdash;that Mawhonic himself had not raced in the Boonta to begin with. These rumors remain unconfirmed. Later Sebulba destroyed his podracer, after the race Mawhonic disappeared.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Mawhonic_Animatic.png|thumb|left|265px|Conceptual art of Mawhonic by Jay Shuster, which depicted the character as a new species, was used as a basis for Mawhonic in early animatics of the film.]]
Mawhonic was created for the [[1999]] theatrical film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], which was directed by [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']] creator [[George Lucas]].<ref name="Insider's Guide">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref> However, Mawhonic's first appearance was in the film's [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]], which was written by [[Terry Brooks]].<ref name="Novelization">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref> Although the character appears as a Gran in the film, Mawhonic was originally conceptualized by artist [[Jay Shuster]] as a never-before-seen alien species with a thin chin and six eyes.<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> This design made it as far as the film's animatic stages, but was ultimately scrapped.<ref name="TPMDVD">{{Film|I}} [[Star Wars home video releases|DVD special features]]</ref> Additionally, even earlier storyboard arts showcased that [[Aldar Beedo]] was meant to be the original racer to be crashed by Sebulba. Later art created by [[Terryl Whitlatch]] portrayed Mawhonic as a thin Gran with large hands, similar to how the character [[Ree-Yees/Legends|Ree-Yees]], from the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''Return of the Jedi'']], appeared. Ultimately, the new alien and the thin Gran designs were combined, using the rotund nature, hands, and feet from the first design and the Gran likeness of the second, creating Mawhonic's final design.<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> Unlike the other Podracer pilots that would appear in ''The Phantom Menace'', Mawhonic was to be portrayed by an actor in a costume. [[Mark Coulier]] was eventually chosen for the role.<ref name="Tatooine Tango">{{SWArchive|url=episode-i/fun/snapshot/2001/02/snapshot20010214.html|series=Episode I Snapshot|text=Tatooine Tango}}</ref> With a method that was used for the creation process of Ree-Yees, Mawhonic's mask was created by the crew of special effects artist [[Nick Dudman]].<ref name="DB" />
